title: 2021 Fall AMC 12B Problem 16
statement: Suppose \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c\) are positive integers such that \[a + b + c = 23\] and \[ \begin{aligned} &\gcd(a, b) + \gcd(b, c) \\ &\quad {}+ \gcd(c, a) = 9. \end{aligned} \] What is the sum of all possible distinct values of \(a^2 + b^2 + c^2?\)

solutions.text:
The condition is symmetric, so assume \(a\le b\le c.\) Then \(a\le7,\) and for each fixed \(a\) we have \(a\le b\le\lfloor\frac{23-a}{2}\rfloor\) and \(c=23-a-b.\) The gcd sum can be evaluated as \[ \begin{aligned} &\gcd(a,b)+\gcd(b,23-a) \\ &\quad {}+\gcd(a,23-b). \end{aligned} \]

Checking these short ranges, the possible gcd sums for \(a=1,2,\ldots,7\) are, respectively, \(\{3,4,13\},\) \(\{4,6,10\},\) \(\{3,5,6,8,9,12\},\) \(\{4,6\},\) \(\{3,7,8,11\},\) \(\{4,6,8\},\) and \(\{9,10\}.\) The value \(9\) occurs only at \((a,b,c)=(3,5,15)\) and \((7,7,9).\)

The triple \((7, 7, 9)\) has \(\gcd\) sum \(7 + 1 + 1 = 9\) and \(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 49 + 49 + 81\) \(= 179.\) The triple \((3, 5, 15)\) has \(\gcd\) sum \(1 + 5 + 3 = 9\) and \(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 9 + 25\) \(+ 225 = 259.\)

The sum of the distinct values is \(179 + 259 = 438.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: By symmetry assume \(a\le b\le c;\) then \(a\le7\) and \(c=23-a-b\)
Use \(\gcd(b,c)=\gcd(b,23-a)\) and check the short range \(a\le b\le\frac{23-a}{2}\)
